title.en: Describe the role of the WTO

say.en: A customer in London calls her bank and is helped by someone in Bengaluru. How did the world become one market like this? In this lesson: Define globalisation.
Explain outsourcing.
Describe the role of the WTO.

body.en: *Globalisation* is the integration of the economy of a country with the world economy, creating greater interdependence. Outsourcing is a major outcome: a company hires regular services from an external source, often from other countries, that it earlier provided itself. With modern IT, services such as call centres, record keeping, accountancy, banking services, music recording and medical transcription are outsourced to India because of low wages and skilled manpower.
body.kn: ಜಾಗತೀಕರಣ ಎಂದರೆ ದೇಶದ ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆಯನ್ನು ವಿಶ್ವ ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸಂಯೋಜಿಸುವುದು. ಹೊರಗುತ್ತಿಗೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಕಂಪನಿ ತಾನೇ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದ ಸೇವೆಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊರಗಿನ, ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿ ವಿದೇಶಿ ಮೂಲದಿಂದ ಪಡೆಯುವುದು. ಕಡಿಮೆ ವೇತನ ಮತ್ತು ಕುಶಲ ಮಾನವ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲದಿಂದ ಭಾರತ ಹೊರಗುತ್ತಿಗೆಯ ತಾಣವಾಗಿದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Outsourcing and the WTO

say.en: A UK firm pays 20 pounds an hour for data entry at home.
An Indian BPO does the same work for 6 pounds an hour. For 10,000 hours the saving is large.
India attracts outsourcing because of low wages and skilled, English-speaking workers.
GATT, set up in 1948, became the WTO in 1995. India is a founder member.
On the board: Outsourcing and the WTO.

prompt.en: Match each term with its meaning.

right.en: Integrating a country's economy with the world economy
A firm buys regular services from an outside source, often abroad
Voice-based services for clients in other countries
Set up in 1948 by 23 countries to cut trade barriers
Founded in 1995 as GATT's successor, with rules for world trade

explanation.en: Cheap communication and skilled workers made India a major destination for outsourcing, while the WTO set rules for opening trade in goods and services.

say.en: Globalisation, outsourcing and the WTO Match each term with its meaning.

body.en: The WTO was founded in 1995 as the successor to the General Agreement on *Trade* and Tariffs (GATT), which was set up in 1948. It aims at a rule-based trading system in which no country can place arbitrary restrictions on trade. It covers trade in goods and services, removes tariff and non-tariff barriers, and India is a founder member.

problem.en: A UK firm pays £20 an hour for data entry at home. An Indian BPO does the same work for £6 an hour. For 10,000 hours of work, how much does the firm save by outsourcing?

answer.en: £1,40,000 saved: low cost with skilled manpower makes India an outsourcing destination.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A UK firm pays £20 an hour for data entry at home. An Indian BPO does the same work for £6 an hour. For 10,000 hours of work, how much does the firm save by outsourcing?

say.en: Let us work through this together. A UK firm pays £20 an hour for data entry at home. An Indian BPO does the same work for £6 an hour. For 10,000 hours of work, how much does the firm save by outsourcing?
Cost in UK equals 10,000 times 20 = £2,00,000.
Cost in India equals 10,000 times 6 = £60,000.
Saving equals 2,00,000 minus 60,000 = £1,40,000.
So the answer is £1,40,000 saved: low cost with skilled manpower makes India an outsourcing destination.
